_expect.name: Buick Rocks and Hitler's Sex Life

co_buick_rocks_and_hitler_s_sex_life.blurb: A small cluster of three short crags on one hillside west of Lyons, in the Buttonrock corner of the St. Vrain canyons. Ten climbs are recorded, mostly traditional lines with two sport routes, and many can also be set up as top-ropes. Grades run from 5.7 up to a single 5.11, with the bulk between 5.7 and 5.10. Routes are brief, generally under 80 feet, and the walk up from the road is short but steep and loose underfoot. The rock quality is middling compared with better-known walls nearby, so this suits a low-key afternoon on moderate gear climbs rather than a destination trip. Climbing is possible most of the year when the weather is dry.

co_keystone_cave_boulder.blurb: A single boulder with a cave feature, filed as one sector of the Sailing Hawks bouldering zone at the edge of Durango. Ten problems are recorded here, nearly all bouldering plus one trad line. The spread is wide: a few easy problems around V1 to V4, a cluster near V5, and several hard ones from V7 to V8, with the one roped route sitting at 5.12. Trails around the zone are well worn, which keeps navigation simple, and the larger Sailing Hawks area is regarded as one of the better places to boulder in town.

co_lower_smoking_section.blurb: A compact cliff in the Goose Creek and Molly Gulch country of the South Platte, set beside the larger Sheeprock formation and handy as a lighter-commitment warm-up. Ten single-pitch routes are listed, six trad and four sport, with a spread from easy 5.6 up through the 5.9 and 5.10 range and a few 5.11s and one 5.12 test piece. Lines are short and rough, mixing slabs, cracks and a few steep sections, and several routes share a common anchor. The walk from the car is brief along a cairned trail. A big overhanging boulder at the top of the trail marks the right-hand end of the wall.

co_center_ring_wall.blurb: A bouldering wall on the East Draw hogback beside Eldorado Springs, near Boulder, and regarded as the best cluster of problems on that band of cliff. Ten problems are recorded, a mix of lines and traverses. They start around V3, take in a few mid-grade problems in the V4 to V6 range, and climb on to some serious hard testpieces in the V10 and V11 range. The East Draw band catches plenty of sun, which makes it a winter-leaning venue. Rattlesnakes are known to shelter on starting holds of some problems, so check holds before pulling on.

co_phat_city.blurb: A small, open crag in the Lincoln Creek drainage on Independence Pass, with wide views to the west. Ten climbs are recorded, six trad and four sport, mainly in the 5.9 to 5.11 range with a single 5.8 and a lone 5.12. Routes are modest in length, with the longer ones around 130 feet. The walk in is an uphill haul of roughly twenty minutes, passing boulders along the creek and following cairns once the trail forks. At this high elevation the crag is a summer and early-autumn proposition, and the exposed setting means little shelter.
